assessments.reasoning: The Oracle HTTPS receipts report HTTP 200, the pinned whole-response digest and both cited range digests. The contiguous ranges [0,8655) and [8655,17310) cover the response. After leading whitespace, the Version 1.0 heading opens the agreement. Section 9 refers to “the jurisdiction specified in a notice contained within the Original Software” for governing law and “the jurisdiction and venue specified in a notice contained within the Original Software” for litigation. Section 10 ends with “Nothing herein is intended or shall be deemed to constitute any admission of liability.” Only three newline characters follow.

The HTTP 200 receipts for text/CDDL-1.0.txt in the SPDX repository report the pinned whole-response digest and both cited range digests. The ranges [0,8257) and [8257,16514) join within the word “that” in Section 3.5. Joining them without a delimiter preserves that word. The file contains the Version 1.0 heading, the same Section 9 notice wording and the same final Section 10 sentence, followed by one newline. The complete normalized comparison passed.

The GitHub Git objects API returned the complete 700-byte response with the cited digest for annotated object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b. Its tag field reads v3.29.0, its target type is commit and its target SHA is 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly matching the revision in the SPDX text URL. This establishes the release mapping independently of the license filename.

challenge.method: Ran the supplied JavaScript unchanged on the newly acquired parts. Its join("") reconstructs each text without inserting a character at the boundary. It folds curly quotation marks to ASCII and compares token counts and every token in order, using space, tab, CR and LF as delimiters. It checks both bodies for the literal notice heading and compares the full publisher text and the prefix before that heading, filtering exact 72-hyphen tokens. The negative control uses spdx.replace("License Grants", "License Conditions") and verifies that this changes the generated token sequence before comparing it with Oracle.
challenge.results: CDDL-OBSERVATION {"byte_identical":false,"normalized_with_notice":true,"normalized_agreement_only":true,"publisher_notice":false,"spdx_notice":false,"separator_count":0,"altered_clause_equal":false}. Both normalized comparisons covered the entire agreement because the publisher text contained neither the notice heading nor the separator. Indentation and blank lines differed. Changing the Section 2 heading broke equality.

limitations: The finding covers only the two pinned text bodies. It establishes normalized equality for CDDL-1.0 at the specified SPDX release. Other editions, project license applicability and approval classification are outside its scope.
The Oracle capture contains no separate California notice. Any project-specific selection of governing law, jurisdiction or venue requires distinct evidence from the project.
The tag provenance rests on the pinned GitHub API response. The API records the annotation as unsigned.
Revalidation is due 2027-05-25, or earlier if Oracle changes or supersedes this representation, the pinned SPDX provenance changes, or the comparison method changes.
